Rashi on Pesachim 75a:12:1.english: A bar of lead - [One] melts it and casts it into her mouth.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:13:1.hebrew: תשרף - כל מיני שריפה משמע, מדלא כתיב באש ונשתוק:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:13:1.english: She shall be burned - It implies all kinds of burning, since [Scripture] did not write “in fire” and stop [there].

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:14:1.hebrew: וכ"ש אש - לשון קושיא הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:14:1.english: And all the more so fire - It is an expression of a difficulty.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:14:2.hebrew: בני אהרן שריפת נשמה וגוף קיים הוא - בסנהדרין (דף נב.), כמין ב' חוטין של אש נכנסו להן בחוטמיהן:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:14:2.english: [With regard to] the sons of Aaron, it is a burning of the soul and the body remains - In Sanhedrin (52a), [it is taught that] something like two threads of fire entered their nostrils.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:15:1.hebrew: חמי האור - רותחין, דהוי נמי שריפת נשמה וגוף קיים:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:15:1.english: [Water] heated by fire - Boiling [water], which is also burning of the soul while the body remains [intact].

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:16:1.hebrew: גזירה שוה - מבני אהרן למה לי? תיפוק מהכא דלא מקפינן חבילי זמורות, דהא "ברור ליה מיתה יפה" בעינן:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:16:1.english: The verbal analogy - from the sons of Aaron, why do I [need it]? Let it be derived from here that we do not surround [her with] bundles of branches, for we require "select for him a kind death."

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:16:2.hebrew: אי לאו גזירה שוה הוה אמינא - על כרחך אש ממש — כגון להקיף חבילי זמורות — בעינן, דאילו שריפת נשמה וגוף קיים לאו שריפה היא, וקרא שריפה אצרכה. ואי משום דרב נחמן, דבעינן מיתה יפה, ה"א נפיש לה חבילים טובא — ירבו לה היסק גדול שתמות מהר:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:16:2.english: If not for the verbal analogy, I would have said - Perforce, we require actual fire — such as surrounding [her with] bundles of branches — since burning the soul while the body remains [intact] is not [considered] burning, and the verse required burning for her. And if [it were only] due to [the statement of] Rav Nachman, that we require a kind death, I would have said: "Let us increase the bundles for her greatly" — [meaning] they should make a large fire for her so that she dies quickly.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:16:3.hebrew: קא משמע לן - גזירה שוה, דשריפת נשמה וגוף קיים נמי שריפה היא, וכיון דשריפה היא, אהני דרב נחמן לאפוקי זמורות ורותחין:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:16:3.english: It teaches us - [i.e.,] the verbal analogy [teaches us] that burning the soul while the body remains is also [considered] burning, and since it is [considered] burning, [the principle of] Rav Nachman is effective to exclude branches and boiling [liquids].

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:17:1.english: But why do I need "in fire" - Since we ultimately include all [methods of] burning.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:17:2.hebrew: אבר מעיקרו - שמוציאין אותו מן הקרקע, רותח הוא בלא תולדת אש:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:17:2.english: Lead from its source - [When] they extract it from the ground, it is boiling without [being] a derivative of fire.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:18:1.hebrew: וכל היכא דכתיב אש - וכתב נמי שריפה בהדיה, לרבויי כל שריפות אתא? בתמיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:18:1.english: And wherever "fire" is written - and "burning" is also written alongside it, does it come to include all [methods of] burning? [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:19:1.hebrew: הכא - כיון דכתיב שריפה ברישא ומשמע כל שריפות, והדר כתב אש, משמע דוקא אש קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:19:1.english: Here - Since "burning" is written first and implies all [types of] burning, and afterward it writes "fire," it implies that it specifically means fire.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:1:1.hebrew: לקיוהא דפירא - איגדו"ר (איגרו"ר: חמיצות), טעם הפרי עומד בו, שלא הוציאו ממנו כלום. ואע"פ שהוחלש מאליו ונתקלקל טעמו, מוציא דם, שכחו בקרבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:1:1.english: The sharpness of the fruit - Aigror [Old French: sourness] — the taste of the fruit remains in it, for nothing has been extracted from it. And even though it became weakened on its own and its taste deteriorated, it draws out blood, for its strength is [still] within it.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:1:2.english: Here, the sharpness of the fruit is not [present] in its pure form - For the first roast absorbed it.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:2:1.hebrew: מנוקבת - עשויה כבריחים כעין שלנו, ויש חלל גדול בין בריח לבריח, ונותן השפוד לרוחבו, וכל הטלה נצלה באויר שבין שני בריחים, שאין בשרו נוגע בברזל:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:2:1.english: Perforated - [It is] made like bars, similar to ours, and there is a large space between one bar and the next, and one places the spit across its width, and the entire lamb is roasted in the air between two bars, so that its meat does not touch the iron.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:3:1.hebrew: לדברי האוסר - בפרק כל שעה (פסחים כו:), רבי אומר: הפת אסורה:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:3:1.english: According to the one who prohibits - In the chapter [entitled] Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 26b), Rabbi says: The bread is prohibited.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:3:2.english: What is [the law] - Here there is no improvement [from] the wood in the bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:4:1.hebrew: צלי אש - קרינא ביה, וגבי עצי איסורא מיהא ניתסר, דהתם לא כתיב מיעוטא:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:4:1.english: Roasted in fire - [Had the verse not written it twice,] we would call it [that], and regarding forbidden wood, at least, it should be forbidden, for there no exclusion is written.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:7:1.hebrew: אאש קפיד רחמנא - וחום התנור תולדת אש הוא, ואם תתן בו בגד, נשרף ונעשה פחם ואש:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:7:1.english: The Merciful One is particular about fire - And the heat of the oven is a derivative of fire, and if you put a garment in it, it burns and becomes coal and fire.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:8:1.hebrew: חתכו - לפסח, ולא הבדיל, אלא חתכו בשנים ושלשה מקומות למהר צלייתו, אינקרני"ר בלע"ז:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:8:1.english: He cut it - [That is,] the Paschal lamb, and did not sever [it completely], rather he cut it in two or three places to hasten its roasting — encrener in Old French.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:9:2.english: Gipsis - It is a type of lime.

Rashi on Pesachim 75a:9:3.hebrew: מניין - שנידון משום מכוה ולא משום שחין. ואף על פי שמכוה ושחין שוין בטומאתן, נפקא מינה דחצי גריס מכת מכוה מחמת אור וחצי גריס מכת שחין — שהוא לקות חום אחר שלא היה מחמת האור — אין מצטרפין. בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף ח.) מפרש:
Rashi on Pesachim 75a:9:3.english: From where - [is it derived] that it is judged as a burn [mikhvah] and not as a boil [sheḥin]. And even though a burn and a boil are equal in their [laws of] ritual impurity, the practical difference [between them] is that half a geris of a burn lesion [caused] by fire and half a geris of a boil lesion — which is an injury [from] another heat that was not caused by fire — do not combine. [This] is explained in [the chapter] Hakol Shoḥatin (Chullin 8a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:10:1.hebrew: הא לאו הכי גחלת לא איקרי אש - נראה לרשב"א דהוה מצי למימר: גלי רחמנא במכוה וגמרינן מיניה, ולא איצטריך לשנויי בע"א, אלא משום לשון אחרון דלעיל. מיהו תימה: אמאי לא משני דרבי איירי בגחלים לוחשות, והכא לא איצטריך לרבויי אלא עוממות דלא איקרי אש, כדמוכח בסמוך? וי"ל: נהי דגחלת דקרא היינו עוממות, סתם גחלת דמשנה ודברייתא הוי לוחשות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:10:1.english: "If not for this, a coal is not called fire" - It appears to Rashba that [the Gemara] could have said: The Merciful One revealed [this] in [the case of] a burn, and we derive [other cases] from it, and it would not have needed to answer differently, except because of the last version above. However, it is astonishing: why does [the Gemara] not answer that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] is speaking of glowing coals, whereas here [it] was only necessary to include dim [coals], which are not called fire, as is proven immediately below? And one can say: Granted that "coal" in Scripture refers to dim [coals], an unspecified "coal" in a Mishnah or a Baraita is glowing [coals].

Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:17:1.hebrew: למעוטי אבר מעיקרו - הקשה ה"ר יוסף: נימא "באש" פרט, "תשרף" כלל, ונעשה כלל מוסף על הפרט, ורבי כל מילי, ואפילו אבר מעיקרו דלא דמי לפרט? וי"ל דכלל ד"תשרף" קאי אפרט, כלומר: במה תשרף? באש; הלכך לא מרבינן מ"תשרף" אלא דומיא דאש, דקאי עילויה, והוי כלל הצריך לפרט, דאמרינן בכיסוי הדם (חולין דף פח:) דאין דנין אותו בכלל ופרט, ריב"א. והקשה רבינו יעקב דאורלינ"ש: אמאי איצטריך קרא למעוטי אבר מעיקרו? הא שמעינן ליה מדאיצטריך "לא תבערו" למעוטי שאין שריפת בת כהן דוחה שבת, מכלל דאין יכול לשורפה באבר מעיקרו; דאי יכול לשורפה בו, א"כ פשיטא דלא דחיא שבת, כיון דיכול לעשות בלא דחיית שבת! ואומר ר"י דלא פירכא היא כלל, דאיצטריך קרא היכא דליכא אבר מעיקרו; דאי לא תימא הכי, תיקשי אמאי איצטריך קרא דלא דחי שבת, כיון שיכול להרתיח פתילה של אבר מערב שבת: [ועיין תוס' יבמות ו: ד"ה טעמא]:
Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:17:1.english: To exclude lead from its source - Rabbi Yosef raised a difficulty: Let us say [that] "in fire" is a specific case [perat], [and] "she shall be burned" is a general statement [kelal], and thus the general statement is added onto the specific case, and it includes everything — even lead from its source, which does not resemble the specific case! And one can answer that the general statement of "she shall be burned" refers to the specific case — that is to say: with what shall she be burned? With fire; therefore, we do not include from "she shall be burned" anything except what is similar to fire, since it refers to it, and it is a general statement that requires a specific case [to clarify it], about which we say in [the chapter] Kisui HaDam (Chullin 88b) that we do not expound it with [the rule of] a general statement and a specific case — Riva. And Rabbeinu Yaakov of Orléans raised a difficulty: Why is a verse needed to exclude lead from its source? We already learn it from the fact that [the verse] "You shall not kindle" is needed to exclude [burning], teaching that the burning of a priest's daughter does not override Shabbat — which implies that one cannot burn her with lead from its source; for if one could burn her with it, then it is obvious that it does not override Shabbat, since one can perform [the execution] without overriding Shabbat! And Ri says that this is not a difficulty at all, for the verse is needed where there is no lead from its source; for if you do not say so, you could [equally] ask why a verse is needed [to teach] that it does not override Shabbat, since one could heat a wick of lead before Shabbat! [And see Tosafot, Yevamot 6b, s.v. Ta'ama]:

Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:18:1.hebrew: באש תשרף לרבות כל שריפות - דתשרף ריבויא הוא, דהוה מצי למיכתב באש תמות:
Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:18:1.english: "In fire she shall be burned" [comes] to include all [methods of] burning - For "she shall be burned" is an amplification, since [Scripture] could have written, "In fire she shall die."

Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:3:1.hebrew: וגרפו ואפה בו את הפת מהו - תימה לריב"א: מאי קבעי? הא קתני סיפא: "בישלה ע"ג גחלים, דברי הכל מותרת", ואפי' למאן דמוקי התם בגחלים עוממות, לא גרע חומו מחום חרס התנור שגרפו! ותירץ ר"י: שאני גחלים, שאין חומן בא מחמת השלהבת אלא מחמת עצמן, ועפרא בעלמא הן; אבל חום התנור שגרפו מחמת חום שלהבת האבוקה בא, שהוא איסור גמור, הילכך מיבעי ליה. ותימה לר"י: כיון דהפת אסור כשאבוקה כנגדו, וחום אבוקה אסור, א"כ כשגרפו ואפה בו את הפת נמי יהא אסור הפת! ופי' ר"י דאפילו כשאבוקה כנגדו לא אסור אלא מדרבנן; ולא משמע כן בשמעתין, וגם לא הוה שייך לפלוגי אי יש שבח עצים בפת אי לא. ובירושלמי דייק: כשהפסח נצלה בתנור והגחלים תחתיו, הלא חום התנור כמו כן מבשלו, והוי צלי מחמת דבר אחר? ומפרש: כי איכא אש, האש נוצח כח התנור, והתנור מצרף חום הגחלים שלא יתפזר:
Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:3:1.english: "And he swept it and baked the bread in it, what is [the halakha]?" - It is astonishing to Riba: What is [Rav Ḥinnana bar Idi] asking? Surely the latter clause [of the Mishnah] teaches: "If one baked it over coals, all agree it is permitted," and even according to the one who establishes [the Mishnah] there as referring to dying coals, their heat is no worse than the heat of the earthenware of the oven that one swept! And Ri resolved [this]: Coals are different, for their heat does not come from the flame, but rather from themselves, and they are mere ash; however, the heat of the oven that one swept comes from the heat of the flame of the torch [i.e., the burning fuel], which is a complete prohibition — therefore he raises the dilemma. And it is astonishing to Ri: Since the bread is prohibited when the torch is opposite it, and the heat of a torch is prohibited, if so, when he swept it and baked the bread in it, the bread should also be prohibited! And Ri explained that even when the torch is opposite it, it is only prohibited rabbinically; however, it does not sound like that in our passage, and furthermore it would not have been relevant to dispute whether there is improvement [imparted by] the wood in the bread or not. And in the Yerushalmi it infers [a difficulty]: When the Paschal lamb is roasted in an oven with the coals beneath it, does not the heat of the oven likewise cook it, such that it is roasted by means of another substance? And [the Yerushalmi] explains: When there is fire, the fire overpowers the force of the oven, and the oven [merely] concentrates the heat of the coals so that it does not disperse.

Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:9:1.hebrew: אין לי אלא שנכוה באש מניין כו' - אע"ג דשחין ומכוה שוין לכל דבר — דשחין ומכוה מטמאים בשבוע אחד, בשיער לבן ובפשיון — מ"מ נפקא מינה לענין צירוף, דשחין ומכוה אין מצטרפין:
Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:9:1.english: "I have only [a case] where it was burned by fire, from where [is it derived]," etc. - Even though a boil [shechin] and a burn [mikhvah] are equal in every respect — for [both] a boil and a burn render [one] impure within one week, through white hair, and through spreading — nevertheless, there is a practical difference with regard to combining [them], for a boil and a burn do not combine [with each other].

Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:9:2.hebrew: נכוה בגחלת בגפסיס כו' - תימה: מה בין גפסים רותח וסיד לחרסו של תנור, דאמרינן לעיל טעמא דכתב רחמנא "צלי אש" שני פעמים, הא לאו הכי "צלי אש" קרינא ביה — והכא איצטריך סיד וגפסיס רותח ריבוייא, אבל מאש לא הוה ידענא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 75a:9:2.english: "If it is burned by a coal... by plaster [gipsis]," etc. - This is astonishing: What is the difference between hot plaster and lime and the earthenware of an oven, regarding which we said above [that] the reason [it is disqualified] is because the Merciful One wrote "roasted with fire" twice — [implying that] were it not for that, we would call it "roasted with fire" — whereas here, hot lime and plaster require an inclusion, and from "fire" [alone] we would not have known [to include them]?
